signals.title: Ducati 998RS faster than Valentino Rossi’s 2002 MotoGP bike goes up for sale
signals.summary: A very rare, fully BSB-spec, championship-winning race bike has gone up for sale in the UK, and it just so happens to be Steve Hislop’s 2002 Ducati 998RS. Remember Steve Hislop’s dominant 2002 BSB season aboard the Monstermob Ducati 998RS? Well, that exact motorcycle is now available to buy. Hislop was victorious eight times with the 998RS that season, also achieving 10 pole positions and 13 fastest laps. Hislop’s bike is a full factory-built 998RS which formed part of a dominant run for the Italian manufacturer in BSB during the late 90s/early 2000s. Ducati machinery won every British Superbike title from 1999 through to 2004, although Hislop became the first rider to win the championship with the new 998 model, which took over from the 996RS. Incredibly, Hislop also broke the Donington Park lap record that season, posting a lap time that was faster than Valentino Rossi’s MotoGP pole lap from the same year. Of course, a direct comparison cannot be made between the two bikes, as the premier class was still using 500cc two-stroke prototypes at the time. However, it still shows just how capable the 998RS was that year to beat a full-spec Grand Prix machine. Offered with the bike is an original race suit and a special helmet used by the Scottish rider, who tragically passed away in July, 2003. Hislop died after suffering a crash while piloting his Robinson R44 helicopter. As well as his exploits in BSB, Hislop was one of the best TT racers of his generation, winning at the iconi

signals.title: Now 81 and living with dementia, Norman Hyde is riding 81 miles to raise money for Dementia UK.
signals.summary: Former Triumph development engineer and record holder Norman Hyde is taking on an 81-mile ride as part of his Ride to Recall campaign for Dementia UK. Not many people can claim to have played a leading role in creating some of the UK’s most famous bikes, set world speed records, and then spent decades making those same bikes faster. Norman Hyde is one of the few people who genuinely can. Now aged 81 and living with dementia, Hyde is using motorcycles once again to raise awareness and money for Dementia UK through his Ride to Recall campaign. Hyde has challenged himself to ride 81 miles, representing his age, without using a Sat-Nav or other electronic navigation aid. The challenge is intended to highlight the importance of memory while raising money for the charity. Hyde has already completed his own 81-mile ride around the North Cotswolds, joined by 20 friends and colleagues from the motorcycle industry. The wider Ride to Recall campaign is running throughout 2026, with other riders encouraged to take on their own 81-mile challenges and support the fundraising effort. For someone whose life has been so closely linked with motorcycles, it's a fitting way to tackle what is clearly a very personal challenge. If you're not familiar with the name, Norman Hyde is one of those characters whose influence on British motorcycling is greater than many modern riders might realise. signals.title: Another London borough wants to start charging bikers to park
signals.summary: Hammersmith & Fulham is consulting on introducing motorcycle parking charges, meaning another London borough could soon make bikers pay to park. There was a time when the biggest advantages of riding a motorcycle into London were that you could avoid the jams, and then park it for free once you got there. One of those advantages is disappearing, with Hammersmith & Fulham now consulting on plans to introduce motorcycle parking charges. At present, motorcycles can park free of charge in shared-use, resident and pay-and-display bays across the borough, although there are some restrictions in the Caxton Village area. The council is now consulting on how motorcycle parking could be changed, with the consultation closing at 5pm on 18 September 2026. The council says its Cabinet approved the introduction of paid motorcycle parking as part of its Parking Strategy back in October 2024. The current consultation is therefore about how the policy should be implemented, rather than whether motorcycles should continue to park for free indefinitely. Hammersmith & Fulham would not be the first London borough to take this route. Westminster currently charges £1 a day for dedicated solo motorcycle bays, with weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual options also available. Camden has also introduced charges, with non-electric motorcycles currently paying £1.30 a day to use its solo motorcycle bays, while fully electric motorcycles pay 66p. signals.title: BMW’s M1000 RR seems to have inspired this new LS2 colourway
signals.summary: LS2 has launched four new colour options aboard its best-selling Advant X modular helmet, two of which look very similar to a pair of BMW superbikes. LS2’s best-selling Advant X motorcycle helmet now has four new Nova colourways to choose from, all of which will cost UK customers £329.99. With the UK currently going through one of its warmest summers in recent memory, there might never have been a better time to buy your next helmet, and if a front-flip lid is what you’re after, LS2’s Advant X could be a contender. The helmet is fully certified to P/J standards, meaning it can be used in both the open and closed position. Additionally, the Advant X is certified to the latest ECE 22.06 safety standards, and is available in two outer shell sizes. In terms of ventilation, ports are located at the chin and forehead, while internal channelling through the EPS liner and large exhaust ports are also part of the lid’s air flow setup. Inside the helmet is a breathable, hypoallergenic comfort liner that is both removable and washable. Furthermore, the helmet weighs just 1600g, which is achieved through the shell’s High Performance Fibreglass Composite (HPFC) construction. When opening the front of the helmet from the closed position, LS2 says “the opening mechanism holds the chin bar close to the face, so there’s less leverage on the neck and head when opening and closing, and it automatically lifts the visor with the chin bar for hassle-free operation”. signals.title: New 1:4-scale Panigale V2 Superquadro Final Edition launched by Pocher
signals.summary: Carl Fogarty has teamed up with large-scale model kit maker Pocher on a new £789 Ducati Panigale V2 Superquadro Final Edition. Four-time World Superbike champion Carl Fogarty has teamed up with Pocher on the release of a new 1:4-scale Ducati Panigale V2 Superquadro Final Edition model kit, which is accompanied by a Ducati Superquadro V2 Engine Model Kit. Fogarty remains Ducati’s most successful WorldSBK rider ever, and his expertise with regards to the Italian brand’s race-spec superbike is unmatched by many. On the other hand, Pocher is a premium large-scale die-cast model kit company that’s also known for their Porsche, Pagani and Ferrari model designs. The release of the new Ducati Panigale V2 Superquadro Final Edition, along with the separate engine kit, is rather special in numerous ways. The first of those is to do with actually ordering the product, as the 99th person who orders the Superquadro Final Edition will be invited to an exclusive Pocher event where they can meet Fogarty. They can also have their model kit signed by the superbike legend. This will take place at The Bike Shed in London. Then there’s the build process, which is estimated to take around 30 hours to complete due to its Skill Level 6 rating, according to Pocher. The new model kit will cost customers £789,99, and it will be available to buy in September. As well as taking around 30 hours to construct, the Final Edition model kit includes more than 700 pieces. signals.title: Husqvarna initiates 2022-2024 enduro and cross-country model recall
signals.summary: Husqvarna has initiated a recall on its 2022-2024 enduro and cross-country models that are fitted with Braktec brake systems, over fears the rear caliper could fail. Husqvarna has confirmed a recall is underway regarding some enduro and cross-country models produced from 2022-2024. The recall is specific to motorcycles that were fitted with Braktec braking systems, as the rear caliper could potentially fail. Husqvarna says that during market monitoring it was deemed that under certain conditions the brake caliper could break due to excessive loads being applied. While the chances of the system breaking are considered “rare”, the company has begun a recall of all models that could be faulty. As a precautionary measure, Husqvarna says “the rear brake caliper, including the caliper bracket, must be replaced on all motorcycles subject to the campaign”. Only a limited number of cases have so far been detected, with all changes set to be made free of charge. That is standard procedure when brands initiate these kinds of recalls, however, customers should be aware that changes can only be made at authorised Husqvarna dealerships. Customers who own one of the affected models will be notified by letter to schedule an appointment. In addition, customers can also check whether their enduro or cross-country motorcycle is affected via the company’s official website. signals.title: Honda’s wild EV Outlier concept has won a Red Dot Design Award, thanks to its radical low-slung design and unusual in-wheel motors.
signals.summary: Honda’s wild EV Outlier Concept has won a 2026 Red Dot Design Award thanks to in-wheel motors and space-age design. Honda’s futuristic EV Outlier Concept has picked up a Red Dot Design Award, with the electric motorcycle concept recognised in the Design Concept category. The award comes less than a year after Honda first showed the Outlier at the Japan Mobility Show in October 2025. It was designed to explore what a motorcycle could look like beyond 2030, rather than simply adapting the conventional motorcycle formula to electric power. The Outlier uses in-wheel motors at both the front and rear, allowing Honda’s designers considerably more freedom with the layout than would be possible with a conventional petrol engine. The result is an extremely low-slung machine with a notably low riding position and unusual proportions. Honda says the design is based around its ‘Precision of Intrinsic Design’ theme for its electric motorcycles, with the Outlier intended to be “unconstrained by boundaries”. The company also says the low seating position is intended to give the rider a more dramatic field of view and a stronger sense of acceleration. There is plenty of concept-bike styling, too, including smooth bodywork and a smoked-clear outer structure intended to expose and highlight the mechanical elements beneath it. signals.title: GIVI X36 modular: designed for every riding segment
signals.summary: The new line-up proposed by GIVI currently features three distinct versions , expertly crafted to satisfy every type of enthusiast while seamlessly blending top-tier technology and comfort. GIVI expands its helmet portfolio with the brand-new X36 modular. At the heart of this project lies the Flip Back system: the chin guard can rotate fully up to 180 degrees, integrating smoothly into the rear shell , making it the ideal solution for riders who effortlessly switch between city streets and long-distance touring. Maximum safety is guaranteed by the dual P/J ECE 22.06 homologation, allowing the helmet to be worn in both open-face and full-face configurations. The range features three versions—Carbon, Fiberglass, and Technopolymer—spanning a total of 19 color and graphic variations. Standing out for its featherlight feel is the Carbon model , which also comes equipped with a complementary 75% smoked visor as standard. The comprehensive standard equipment features an anti-scratch visor pre-set for a Pinlock lens (included), an integrated sun visor, and a shell available in two sizes.
